title.rendered: This Is the Day — Morning Devotional

excerpt.rendered: Saturday morning. Before the noise begins — choose joy. Today’s devotional on Psalm 118:24 and why rejoicing is a decision, not a feeling.

content.rendered:
📖 Scripture

“This is the day that the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.”
— Psalm 118:24 (ESV)

📝 Message

Saturday morning. The pace is different. The obligations are lighter. And yet for many people, Saturday is not a day of joy — it is a day of catching up, of quiet anxiety about the week ahead, of scrolling through the noise that Monday will bring.

Psalm 118:24 is a deliberate, intentional choice. The psalmist does not say: this happens to be a good day, so let us enjoy it. He says: this is the day the Lord has made — and therefore let us rejoice. The rejoicing is grounded not in the quality of the day but in its Source.

God made this day. He made this Saturday. He knew you would wake up in it, with whatever you woke up carrying — the unresolved thing, the lingering worry, the tiredness that a night’s sleep did not fully fix. And He still made it with purpose. He still filled it with possibility. He still placed in it mercies that are specifically yours to find.

The word “rejoice” in Hebrew is gil — to spin around, to leap for joy, to express exuberance. This is not a quiet, polite acknowledgment that the day exists. It is a full-bodied, whole-hearted response to the fact that God made it — and that He is in it.

You do not have to feel like rejoicing to choose it. In fact, the command exists precisely because rejoicing is not always the natural first response. It is a posture you take. A decision you make before the day has a chance to talk you out of it.

So before the noise begins — before the phone, before the list, before the week reaches back to claim you — say it out loud: This is the day the Lord has made. I will rejoice and be glad in it.

Mean it. Watch what happens.

🙏 Prayer

Lord, I choose joy today — not because everything is easy but because You made this day and You are in it. Open my eyes to the goodness You have placed in this Saturday. Let me not miss the mercies hidden in the ordinary. Teach me to rejoice on purpose, by decision, as an act of trust in You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

This is the day the Lord has made and I will rejoice and be glad in it. Joy is my choice today. I receive this Saturday as a gift from God — full of His purpose, His presence, and His mercy. I will not let worry steal what God has given. I rejoice in this day with a grateful and open heart.

📖 Further Reading

  • Psalm 118:19–29 — Read the full context of this verse of triumph
  • Nehemiah 8:10 — The joy of the Lord is your strength
  • Philippians 4:4 — Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say rejoice
  • James 1:2–4 — Count it all joy when you face trials of various kinds
  • Habakkuk 3:17–18 — Yet I will rejoice in the Lord
  • John 15:11 — That my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be full
